title: Maximising ₹5 Lakh in a 444-Day Special FD: PSU Bank Returns
description: Special Fixed Deposits (FDs) offer higher interest rates for specific, non-standard tenures like 444 days. Public Sector Banks (PSUs) frequently introduce the.

faq.a: A 444-day special FD is a fixed deposit offered by banks for a specific, non-standard tenure of 444 days, usually with an attractive, often higher, interest rate compared to regular FDs.

faq.q: Are special FDs offered by all banks?
faq.a: No, special FDs are typically offered by banks for limited periods, often to meet specific liquidity requirements or to compete in the market. Not all banks offer them concurrently, and the tenures can vary.

faq.q: How is interest on FDs taxed?
faq.a: Interest earned on FDs is fully taxable as "Income from Other Sources" and is added to your total income, then taxed according to your applicable income tax slab rate.

faq.q: Can I withdraw money from a special FD early?
faq.a: Most FDs, including special ones, allow premature withdrawal, but it usually comes with a penalty. Banks typically deduct a percentage (e.g., 0.50% to 1%) from the contracted interest rate for early withdrawals.

faq.q: Are senior citizens eligible for higher rates on special FDs?
faq.a: Yes, most banks offer an additional interest rate benefit, typically 0.25% to 0.75% higher, for senior citizens (aged 60 and above) on both regular and special fixed deposits.

Quarterly compounding means that the interest earned on your fixed deposit is calculated and added to your principal amount every three months. Subsequent interest calculations are then based on this new, larger principal, leading to faster growth.
